title: The Department copy owed after filling an out-of-state Schedule II prescription
rule_summary: Where a Schedule II prescription is filled under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d) (a nonnarcotic Schedule II prescription from an out-of-state practitioner) or s. 18(d1/2) (a narcotic Schedule II prescription from a practitioner registered in Maine or a state contiguous with the commonwealth), the pharmacist SHALL, WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER FILLING the prescription, DELIVER TO THE DEPARTMENT A COPY OF EACH SUCH SCHEDULE II PRESCRIPTION. The copy SHALL NOT INCLUDE THE NAME AND ADDRESS OF THE PATIENT for whom the prescription was issued, and neither the copy nor the information on it is a public record within M.G.L. c. 4, s. 7; both are subject to the restrictions in M.G.L. c. 66A, s. 2. Both subsections state this duty in the same terms. Neither subsection authorizes the out-of-state practitioner to possess, administer or dispense controlled substances under s. 9 or to practise within the commonwealth, and neither authorizes mail order pharmacies.
exam_relevance: Tests a duty that arises only after the fill and only on the out-of-state Schedule II pathways, and that runs on a 30-day clock unrelated to the five-day window governing the prescription itself.

authority.name: Out-of-state nonnarcotic Schedule II prescriptions, Department copy
Out-of-state narcotic Schedule II prescriptions, Department copy

numeric_facts.fact: Pharmacist delivery of the Department copy after filling an out-of-state Schedule II prescription
numeric_facts.conditions: Measured from the filling, not from the prescription issue date

exceptions: The copy is anonymised: the patient's name and address are excluded.
The copy is not a public record and is subject to the M.G.L. c. 66A, s. 2 restrictions.
common_confusions: Measuring the 30 days from the prescription issue date rather than from the filling.
Carrying the duty across to out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescriptions, where the statute does not state it.
Sending the copy with patient identifiers, which the subsections expressly exclude.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d) and s. 18(d1/2) read verbatim in the current official publication on 2026-09-10. Added because SG-MA-OUTSTATE-PRESCRIPTIONS taught the out-of-state Schedule II pathway without the post-fill reporting duty the same subsections impose, and no canonical rule carried it. Independent audit still required.
